children: Taiwan's central bank kept its benchmark interest rate on hold on Thursday, as expected, given the strong performance of the tech-focused economy and relatively mild inflation, and also raised its growth outlook for the year.
The central bank's decision to leave the benchmark discount rate (TWINTR=ECI) at 2% aligned with forecasts in a Reuters poll, where 28 of 31 economists projected no change in monetary policy.
The central bank raised its 2026 economic growth forecast to 11.48% from the previous prediction of 9.45% given in June. For next year, it forecast the economy will slow to an expansion of 5.82%.
Taiwan's economy grew 8.68% in 2025, its fastest rate in 15 years, buoyed by high demand for semiconductors used in artificial intelligence applications from companies such as Nvidia
The central bank also slightly raised its consumer price index (CPI) forecast for this year to 2.03%, up from its June forecast of 1.91%, but foresaw it dropping to 1.83% next year.
Taiwan's rate decision follows a move by the US Federal Reserve on Wednesday to raise interest rates by 25 basis points and flag more hikes in the coming months.
